title: Onboard per-model KV eviction signals and publish long-context profile variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Customer workloads with heavy long-context tails show abrupt latency spikes and quality regressions when the serving runtime evicts KV cache entries aggressively. Current catalog exposes a single 'kv_profile' per model that conflates retention and latency trade-offs.

Goal:
Create a first-class per-model KV eviction metadata signal and publish multiple performance profile variants for each onboarded model (e.g., retention-optimized, latency-optimized, cost-optimized). Wire profile selection into version pinning and rollout rules so customers with long-context SLAs get deterministic behavior without manual config.

Scope and deliverables:
- Define a compact KV eviction signal schema (string+numeric fields) that captures: hot-key retention score, per-layer KV footprint ratio, recommended retention window, and preferred eviction policy (LRU/TTL/hybrid).
- Extend the onboarding pipeline to compute eviction signals from offline traces and microbenchmarks across sequence-length buckets (0-128,129-512,513-2048,2049+).
- Produce three canonical profile variants per model: retention-optimized, balanced, latency-optimized. Each variant includes: throughput/latency curves, token-cost estimate, cache hit-rate expectation.
- Publish variant metadata to the model catalog and surface profile tags in the Console and API (model.profile=retention/balanced/latency).
- Add deterministic version-pinning rules so a customer that pins to `retention-optimized` receives the matching model binary or a compatible fallback if exact quantization/version unavailable.
- Update rollout logic: canary + staged promotion will validate latency and cache hit SLOs against the selected profile's expectations.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Eviction signal schema documented in the onboarding spec (Confluence) and stable.
2) For three canonical open models (open-Llama-13B, redwood-base-7B, mpt-30b), we have published three profile variants and corresponding perf curves in the catalog.
3) Console and API expose `model.profile` and customers can request a profile at create/model-inference time.
4) Version-pinning honors profile compatibility (tests for fallback behavior exist and pass in CI).
5) Telemetry emits per-request: chosen-profile, catalog-version, observed-KV-hit-rate, eviction-events; dashboards created in Grafana.
6) No regression in short-context latency SLOs for default customers during rollout (compare baseline to canary).

Non-goals:
- Full auto-tuner that rewrites eviction policies in prod (follow-ups).
- Per-request adaptive eviction decisions (later initiative).
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage complete. Spoke with Product (Nora) — customers with long-document search and summarization are highest priority. Will produce schema proposal by 2026-03-05.

2026-03-05 - Mateo Klein: Draft schema uploaded: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/KV+Eviction+Signal+Schema (see section 2). Decided on numeric retention_score (0-100) and retention_window_tokens field. Pushed small RFC in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding/pull/214
2026-03-07 - Eng Review (K. Huang): Asked for an additional per-layer footprint metric to account for attention-kv imbalance. Mateo updated schema and added unit tests in PR #214.

2026-03-09 - Performance experiments: ran long-context microbenchmarks across the 4 seq buckets for open-Llama-13B. Observed 28% drop in cache hit-rate when eviction_window < 1024 tokens; retention-optimized profile recovers throughput by preallocating larger KV retention windows.

2026-03-10 - Design (Lina Gomez): Console UX mockups uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bMockups Profiles will be shown as a dropdown with quick SLO badges (latency/cost/hit-rate). Lina suggested adding an inline tooltip explaining trade-offs.

2026-03-11 - Mateo Klein: Integration spike: added model.profile tag to model registry and implemented simple profile selection logic in the router. Integration tests added (tests/router/test_profile_fallback.py). Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/980 (WIP).

2026-03-12 - QA (R. Singh): Found a flaky case where fallback from quantized variant to fp16 caused loss in expected hit-rate metric; added a blocking test and created ENG-14958 to investigate quantized compatibility gaps.
